In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
digital skills can be considered as a "field", in the sociological sense, in which a constant and dynamic interaction between the different elements that make it up, is taking place.
, in order to grasp and understand digital skills, we should not only rely on top down models, but also on micro ethnography and bottom up analysis.

digital skills can be considered a complex and multidisciplinary field that is still in the making, and which requires a multidimensional approach, capable of integrating top down and bottom up methodologies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the future of digital skills is not only in the formalization of the skills, but also in the ability to capture the informal, the non standardized, the local.

of "digital competences for the 4.0 world" that are not limited to the digital skills, but that also include the social and cultural skills, as well as those that are necessary to interpret the new digital environment and its changes.

, in the field of the digital skills, the most interesting research and innovation trends are those that are capable of integrating the standardization of skills, with the ability to interpret, through ethnographic tools, the informal and emerging practices of digital work.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a combination of different methods, and the use of a "bottom up" approach, is needed in order to capture a dynamic and constantly evolving phenomenon such as digital skills.

, in the digital field, the bottom up approach is necessary to complement and complete top down approaches, in order to create a more complete and realistic vision of the digital competences for the future.
it is important not to lose sight of the bottom up dimension of digital skills and the informal practices of digital working in "industry 5.0" contexts.
